nodes.label: Currency Conversion System
nodes.rationale: Uses real-time rates from exchangerate-api.com with fallback rates for offline use, and documents the original amount/rate in expense notes for auditability.

nodes.label: Spanish Date Parsing
nodes.rationale: Supports Spanish month abbreviations and full names plus multiple date formats so BAC's Spanish-language emails parse reliably.

nodes.label: Automatic Categorization System
nodes.rationale: Uses prioritized rule types (vendor_exact, vendor_contains, keyword_contains) evaluated highest-priority-first to auto-assign expense categories.

nodes.label: SQLite Database System
nodes.rationale: Vendor keywords, categories, and categorization rules were migrated to SQLite for more efficient and maintainable data management than hardcoded Python structures.

nodes.label: Idempotency / Duplicate Prevention (1.1)
nodes.rationale: Flagged as the single highest-risk issue: re-running the app currently creates duplicate rows in Sheets because there is no record of already-processed emails.

nodes.label: FILTER_BY_MONTH hardcoded config
nodes.rationale: Hardcoded to "2025/09" and outdated; should default to the current month or None.

nodes.label: Fallback exchange rates in config_manager.py
nodes.rationale: Rates are ~5-10% off vs 2026 rates; needs a scheduled refresh or a user-editable config.json instead of source-code changes.

nodes.label: Date Parsing Fallback Bug (1.3)
nodes.rationale: date_parser.py silently falls back to today's date when parsing fails, assigning the wrong date to an expense instead of raising an error; should raise ExpenseParsingError with the unparsed string.

nodes.label: Retry Logic for Transient Failures (1.4)
nodes.rationale: Gmail and Sheets API calls have no retry, so a single rate-limit response or timeout silently fails the expense; propose exponential backoff (3 attempts).

nodes.label: Specific Error Types (2.2)
nodes.rationale: A generic "Failed to parse email" message tells you nothing; splitting into specific error types surfaces the actual failure reason in the GUI status panel and log.

nodes.label: Rate Limiting Awareness (2.3)
nodes.rationale: The current 0.5s fixed delay ignores HTTP 429 responses; propose checking status codes and backing off dynamically, plus tracking calls toward exchangerate-api.com's 1500/month limit.

nodes.label: Persist GUI Config (3.1)
nodes.rationale: Config changes in the GUI aren't saved and reset on next launch; propose writing to config.json on Save and loading it at startup, falling back to config.py defaults.

nodes.label: Configurable Sheets Columns (3.2)
nodes.rationale: Column range B:E is hardcoded in sheets_manager.py; propose a configurable column mapping.

nodes.label: Email Recovery Mode (3.3)
nodes.rationale: Only unread emails are fetched; if one was marked read prematurely it's unrecoverable. Propose a reprocess date-range option using Gmail after:/before: queries, skipping already-logged email IDs.

nodes.label: Multi-Bank / Multi-Account Support (3.4)
nodes.rationale: The Gmail query is hardcoded to BAC Credomatic's sender/subject; refactor into a BankProfile configuration stored in the database so a second bank can be added without changing source code.

nodes.label: Test Coverage (4.1)
nodes.rationale: Most files under test/ are empty stubs; priority order is date_parser (6 format patterns + Spanish months), expense_parser (8 amount regex patterns), currency_converter (caching, fallback, API failure), using pytest + unittest.mock to avoid real credentials.

nodes.label: Secrets Out of Source Tree (4.3)
nodes.rationale: src/credentials.json should not be committed; add it to .gitignore and provide a credentials.json.example template, and document the OAuth setup in README.

nodes.label: config.py to config.json migration (4.4)
nodes.rationale: Having user-specific values (Spreadsheet ID, month filter) in a .py file means any edit is a code change; migrate to a config.json in the project root, editable without touching Python files.

nodes.label: Category Rule Editor in GUI (5.4)
nodes.rationale: Adding/editing categorization rules currently requires the admin_database.py CLI or direct SQLite access; a CRUD table in the Config tab would make the app self-contained for non-technical users.
